rows.ts_value: The Company may request 1-year extensions by notice no earlier than 60 and no later than 30 days before any anniversary of the Closing Date. Lenders respond no later than 15 days before, and the Agent notifies the Company no later than 10 days before. The extension is effective if MORE THAN 50% of the Facility Amount is extended or committed by Extending Lenders and new Lenders. Declining Lenders terminate at the existing date and may be replaced. No conditions to extension are stated. There is no term-out option.
rows.ts_quote: provided that more than 50% of the Facility Amount under the 5-Year Facility is extended or otherwise committed to by Extending Lenders and any new Lenders.
rows.ca_value: Section 2.19: request at least 30 and not more than 60 days before any anniversary of the Effective Date for a one-year extension. Lenders respond at least 15 days before, and silence is deemed non-consent. The Agent notifies the Company not later than 10 days before. The extension is effective if Lenders holding AT LEAST 50% of the Revolving Credit Commitments consent, subject to the Section 3.03 conditions. Because the 3.03(a)(i) carve-out of the no-MAC (4.01(e) last sentence), litigation (4.01(f)) and other reps applies only to Borrowings and issuances, all representations, including no MAC and no litigation, must be true on each Extension Date, and no Default may exist. Non-Consenting Lenders terminate at the unextended date. Assuming Lenders must take at least $25,000,000. There is no term-out option.
rows.ca_quote: Lenders having Revolving Credit Commitments equal to at least 50% of the Revolving Credit Commitments in effect immediately prior to the Extension Date consent in writing to a requested extension
rows.ca_location: Section 2.19(a)-(d) PDF pp.60-62; Section 3.03 PDF pp.68-69
rows.explanation: The notice windows, 1-year increment, unlimited number of extensions and treatment of declining lenders match. The consent threshold falls from 'more than 50%' in the TS to 'at least 50%' in the CA, which favours the borrower only at exactly 50%. Against that, the CA adds lender-favourable terms the TS does not state: deemed non-consent for silent Lenders, a $25M minimum for Assuming Lenders, and a full Section 3.03 bring-down on each Extension Date that includes the no-MAC and litigation reps. The net effect is mixed.

rows.ts_value: No more than once a year, the Company may increase commitments in minimum increments of $25,000,000, up to a maximum of $4,500,000,000 ($3,500,000,000 after the Spin Off). The condition is that no default or event of default has occurred and is continuing. The Company may offer the increase to (x) existing lenders, who have no obligation to participate, or (y) third-party institutions. Allocations are agreed among the Company, the Agent, each L/C issuer and the swing line lender. New lenders must be reasonably acceptable to the Agent, L/C issuers and swing line lender, with a minimum of $25,000,000 each.
rows.ts_quote: The Company will have the right, no more than once a year, to increase the Facility Amount of the 5-Year Facility, in minimum increments of $25,000,000, up to a maximum Facility Amount of $4,500,000,000 (or following the consummation of the Spin Off, $3,500,000,000)
rows.ca_value: Section 2.18: not more than once in any calendar year, increases of $25,000,000 or an integral multiple. The Increase Date must be at least 90 days before the earliest scheduled Termination Date. Caps are $4,500,000,000 before the Spin-Off Date and $3,500,000,000 on and after it. Section 3.03 conditions must be met on the request date and the Increase Date: all reps true in all material respects (including no MAC and litigation, because the 3.03(a)(i) carve-out applies only to Borrowings and issuances) and no Default. The request goes first to existing Lenders (2.18(b)). The Company may approach Eligible Assignees only for any shortfall (2.18(c)). Allocation among over-subscribing Lenders is agreed between the Company and the Agent, and each increased commitment needs Issuing Bank and Swing Line Bank approval, not to be unreasonably withheld. Eligible Assignees must be approved by each Issuing Bank and Swing Line Bank and commit $25,000,000 or an integral multiple. Board resolutions and an opinion are required.
rows.ca_quote: in no event shall the aggregate amount of the Revolving Credit Commitments at any time exceed (x) prior to the Spin-Off Date, $4,500,000,000 and (y) on and after the Spin-Off Date, $3,500,000,000
rows.ca_location: Section 2.18(a)-(d) PDF pp.58-60; Section 3.03 PDF pp.68-69
rows.explanation: The caps ($4.5bn, or $3.5bn after the Spin-Off), the $25M increase sizing and voluntary lender participation match. The CA adds lender-favourable conditions the TS does not state. These are a full rep bring-down (including no MAC) on top of no Default, a cut-off 90 days before maturity, resolution and opinion deliverables, and an effective right of first offer for existing Lenders, since third parties can be approached only for the shortfall. The TS lets the Company offer to existing Lenders or third parties. New-lender commitments must also be $25M multiples rather than just at least $25M. The calendar-year frequency limit is a neutral reading of 'once a year'.

Term SOFR, EURIBOR, SONIA (published on the fifth business day preceding) and TIBOR each have a zero floor. rows.ca_value: Base Rate is the highest of (a) the Federal Funds Rate (zero floor) + 1/2 of 1%, (b) the BofA prime rate, and (c) Term SOFR + 1.00%. Term SOFR (CME screen, 2 U.S. Government Securities Business Days prior) has a zero floor. The CA's step-up applies to Revolving Credit Advances rather than 'each Advance', so swing line advances are largely outside it. This is a small offset in the borrower's favour, because unpaid swing lines are refinanced into revolving advances.

Excludes Debt owed to institutions holding sufficient deposits, and Debt of China/India/CIS/Turkey subsidiaries (unsupported, government-caused, assets not over $500m individually or $650m collectively). rows.ca_value: 6.01(a): Revolving principal when due; Swing Line principal, interest, commitment fees and LC commissions within 3 Business Days; other amounts within 30 days unless contested in good faith and placed in Escrow. (b) Reps incorrect in any material respect. (c) Company repudiates the guarantee. (d) Breach of 5.01(h)(v) with no grace; breach of 5.02(a) uncured 30 days after notice; other covenants uncured 30 days after notice or officer knowledge. (e) Cross-payment default or acceleration of Debt of at least $500m in aggregate of the Company or a Material Subsidiary, with the deposit carve-out, a carve-out for Spin-Off and refinancing prepayments, and the Exempt Countries carve-out ($500m / $650m book value). (f) Bankruptcy of the Company or a Material Subsidiary (30 days for involuntary cases), with the Exempt Countries carve-out. (g) A money judgment over $500m against the Company or a Material Subsidiary, with enforcement begun and 10 consecutive days unstayed, with the Exempt Countries carve-out. (h) A non-monetary MAE judgment unstayed for 60 days. (i) Licences revoked. (j) ERISA: over $500m, withdrawal liability over 6% of Net Tangible Assets, or multiemployer contribution increase over $500m. Acceleration by Majority Lenders; automatic on US bankruptcy.
rows.ca_quote: (g) Any judgment or order for the payment of money in excess of $500,000,000 shall be rendered against the Company or any of its Material Subsidiaries
rows.ca_location: Section 6.01(a)-(j), PDF pp.78-81
rows.explanation: The $500m thresholds, the Exempt Countries carve-out ($500m / $650m) and the payment grace periods match. The CA is looser than the TS wording in several ways: (1) judgments are tested per judgment, not 'individually or in the aggregate', and also require enforcement proceedings plus a 10-consecutive-day unstayed period; (2) cross-default, bankruptcy and judgment tests apply only to the Company and Material Subsidiaries (10% revenue/asset test, plus each Designated Subsidiary); (3) swing line principal gets a 3-Business-Day grace period; (4) contested amounts placed in Escrow are excluded; (5) cross-default excludes intra-group Debt and payments barred by law, carves out Spin-Off and refinancing prepayments, and counts guaranteed or secured third-party Debt only when the Company or Subsidiary itself fails to pay; (6) the Exempt Countries carve-out is extended to the bankruptcy event, where the TS applied it only to cross-default and judgments. In the Lenders' favour, the CA limits the Exempt Countries carve-out to Subsidiaries (TS: 'subsidiary or affiliate'), adds a cross-default limb for required prepayment, redemption or repurchase offers, and adds guarantee repudiation, non-monetary judgment, licence revocation and two further ERISA triggers (withdrawal liability over 6% of Net Tangible Assets; multiemployer contribution increase over $500m). On balance the changes favour the Borrower.

The TS also mentions a 364-Day Facility that this CA does not cover. CA: a new standalone "FIVE YEAR CREDIT AGREEMENT" dated as of March 6, 2026 (SEC Exhibit 10.2, Execution Version). Parties: Honeywell International Inc. as Borrower, and Bank of America, N.A. as Administrative Agent and Swing Line Agent. Amount: U.S. $4,000,000,000. It is not an amendment. Instead it requires repayment and termination of the March 18, 2024 agreement as a closing condition (Section 3.01(g)). Article VIII numbering in the CA is irregular: there are two Sections 8.07 (Resignation of Agent at p.88 and Non-Reliance at p.90), followed by 8.08 Other Agents, 8.09 Lender ERISA and 8.10 Erroneous Payments (pp.90-91). Limitations: (1) The CA PDF (142 pages) ends at the signature pages. Schedule I (Commitments), Schedule 2.01(b), Schedule 9.02 and Exhibits A-F (forms of Note, Designation Letter, opinions and so on) are listed in the table of contents but are not in the file. Per-lender commitments, swing line and LC commitment allocations, and the agreed forms therefore could not be reconciled. (2) The Existing 5-Year Agreement was not provided. Where the TS defers to it (basket levels, grace periods, Rating Condition, Eligible Assignee, Defaulting Lender provisions), the CA could only be checked against the TS's express wording, and "substantially similar / no less favorable" could not be verified. (3) Group A economic terms (amount, maturity, accordion, extension, sublimits, benchmarks, pricing grid, fees, prepayments, interest mechanics, benchmark replacement) are excluded here under the instructions. Borrowing notice and minimums were not clearly in either group and are covered in added row X17, where the Term SOFR notice period differs (TS 3 business days, CA 2 Business Days). (4) The TS has no financial covenant, sustainability/ESG pricing, ratings condition precedent or cashless-rollover terms, and the CA has no leverage, coverage, net worth or EBITDA test, so no rows were raised for those. All ts_quote and ca_quote fields were checked mechanically against the text files (whitespace collapsed) and appear verbatim.
